# Intractify — Private Cloud Browser Platform (Full Reference)

> Intractify is a pre-launch cloud-based platform providing fully isolated, ephemeral browser sessions. The browser runs entirely on cloud infrastructure — your device is only a viewport. The container is destroyed when the session ends. No local traces. No pricing or billing yet.

---

## Product Identity

- **Official name**: Intractify
- **Company legal name**: Intractify Technologies
- **Product type**: SaaS — Security Application, Privacy Application, Web Application
- **Primary use case**: Private web browsing via isolated cloud containers
- **Secondary use cases**: Sandboxed browsing, credential isolation, malware-safe browsing, research
- **Founded**: 2025
- **Website**: https://intractify.com
- **App**: https://app.intractify.com
- **Industry terms**: Remote Browser Isolation (RBI), Browser Isolation, Ephemeral Browsing, Container Isolation

---

## How Intractify Works (Technical)

### Session Lifecycle
```
User launches a session →
Fresh container boots a Chromium browser in the cloud →
Pixel stream to user viewport over WebSocket (noVNC) →
User browses →
Session ends (manual / idle / max duration) →
Container destroyed →
No local traces on the user's device
```

### Isolation Architecture
- **Runtime**: per-session container
- **Isolation unit**: Own filesystem and network per session — no cross-tenant shared state by construction
- **Browser**: Chromium in a disposable container
- **Streaming**: pixel stream over WebSocket (viewport only — not screen recording)
- **Session start**: cold start, provisioned on demand to enforce concurrency limits

### What Is Never Logged
- URLs visited
- Passwords or form inputs
- Screen or visual content
- Keyboard or mouse input
- Cookies, local storage, session storage
- Downloaded files
- Browsing history

### What Is Stored
- Session metadata (start, end, duration) for session management and usage display
- Account profile (via Clerk auth provider)

---

## Privacy & Data Retention

| Data Type | Retention Period | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Browsing activity (URLs, passwords, history) | Never stored | Zero retention by architecture |
| Session metadata (start, end, duration) | While active | Used for session management |
| Account profile (name, email) | Active + deletion on request | Via Clerk auth provider |
| Cookies, downloads, cache | 0 seconds after session end | Destroyed with container |

## Status

Intractify is **pre-launch**. There is no billing or pricing of any kind. Anyone can join the waitlist.

## Comparison: Intractify vs. Alternatives

### vs. VPN
| | VPN | Intractify |
|---|---|---|
| Hides your IP | Yes | Yes — the browser does not run on your device |
| Browser runs on your device | Yes — can be fingerprinted | No — browser runs in the cloud |
| History after session | On your device | None — container destroyed |
| Malware risk | Your device at risk | Browser container is isolated |

### vs. Incognito / Private Mode
| | Incognito | Intractify |
|---|---|---|
| Runs locally | Yes | No |
| Your device's attributes visible to sites | Yes | No — the browser is not on your device |
| History deleted after session | Yes | Never created |
| IP hidden | No | Yes — the browser is not on your device |

### vs. Tor Browser
| | Tor Browser | Intractify |
|---|---|---|
| Browser runs on your device | Yes | No |
| Speed | Slow (relay routing) | Direct stream |
| Your device exposed to page content | Yes | No |
| Session footprint | On your device | Container destroyed on end |

Note: Intractify does not hide the fact that you are using a remote browser, and it does not alter the session container's own fingerprint.

---

## Technical Specifications

- **Local traces post-session**: 0
- **Browser engine**: Chromium
- **Container runtime**: per-session container per session
- **Streaming protocol**: WebSocket (noVNC)
- **Encryption in transit**: TLS 1.3
- **Encryption at rest**: AES-256
- **Auth provider**: Clerk
- **Cache/queue infrastructure**: Upstash

## Glossary of Key Terms

**Browser Isolation**: Running the web browser in a remote cloud container rather than on the user's device. Only a visual stream reaches the user — threats and trackers cannot reach the actual device.

**Ephemeral Browser**: A browser session with no persistent storage. All session data is destroyed when the session ends — by architectural design, not by a delete operation.

**Container Isolation**: Each session runs in its own container with a private filesystem and network — preventing state leakage between sessions.

**Zero-Log Architecture**: System design where no browsing activity is ever written to storage. Intractify never stores browsing content.

**Remote Browser Isolation (RBI)**: Architecture where browsing is executed in a remote environment and only visual output is delivered to the user.

**Browser Fingerprinting**: A tracking technique that identifies users by combining browser attributes — screen resolution, fonts, canvas rendering, WebGL output, audio processing — without using cookies. Because the browser runs on our infrastructure, none of these are read from your device. The session container's own fingerprint is not masked.

---

## Frequently Asked Questions

**Q: Does Intractify store my browsing history?**
A: No. Intractify never logs URLs visited, passwords typed, screen content, keyboard input, mouse movements, cookies, or any browsing activity.

**Q: What happens when a session ends?**
A: The container running your browser is destroyed. Cookies, history, cache, downloads — all gone with it. A new session always starts fresh.

**Q: How is Intractify different from a VPN?**
A: A VPN hides your IP but the browser still runs on your device, which can still be fingerprinted. Intractify runs the entire browser in the cloud — the site never reads your device's attributes.

**Q: How is Intractify different from Incognito mode?**
A: Incognito mode runs locally on your device and only clears history after the session. Your device's attributes are still visible to websites. Intractify runs the browser in an isolated cloud container, so the site never sees your device at all.

**Q: Can a website tell I'm using a remote browser?**
A: The browser runs on our infrastructure, so a site cannot read your real IP, OS, fonts, or hardware. Intractify does not mask the session's own fingerprint and does not claim that the remote browser is undetectable.

**Q: Does Intractify have pricing?**
A: Not yet. Intractify is pre-launch. Joining the waitlist is free and requires no payment.

**Q: Does Intractify work on mobile?**
A: Yes. Intractify runs in any modern web browser — desktop or mobile. Because the session runs in the cloud and streams to your browser, there is nothing to install.

**Q: How fast does a session start?**
A: Sessions are provisioned on demand, so a cold start can take up to a few minutes. There is no claim of sub-5-second starts.

**Q: What is browser fingerprinting?**
A: Browser fingerprinting is a tracking technique that identifies users by combining browser attributes — screen resolution, fonts, canvas rendering, WebGL output, audio processing — without using cookies. Because the browser runs on our infrastructure, none of these are read from your device.
